messages:
oliver: Quick context — console dashboards (quotas + per-route p99) are doing expensive joins against the envelope table and we keep hitting slow queries on peak. I want to propose using a materialized counter MV that aggregates by route_id + window (1m/1h) and sharding by tenant to cut query time and remove the hot join path. Thoughts?

raj: +1 on idea, curious about write amplification and cardinality explosion. How are you thinking about sparsity (lots of routes with no traffic) and shard keys?

oliver: Good Q. Plan is to use sparse MV population: only create rows for route/time buckets that have data. Shard by tenant_id % 32 for storage layout so a single tenant with many routes can be spread. For the common case (small customers) layout stays compact.

sasha: Can you paste the MV DDL you imagine? also need to verify refresh strategy — concurrent, incremental?

oliver: Sketch:

```
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW console.route_counters_minute
  WITH (timescaledb.compress, timescaledb.compress_orderby = 'route_id, minute') AS
SELECT tenant_id, route_id, minute_bucket, sum(token_count) as tokens, count(*) as requests
FROM console.envelopes
GROUP BY tenant_id, route_id, minute_bucket;
CREATE INDEX ON console.route_counters_minute (tenant_id, route_id, minute_bucket);
```

Then populate via streaming aggregator: small consumer reads envelope stream, aggregates into minute buckets, writes upserts into a counters table that backs the MV (or we can implement MV-like table directly). Refresh strategy: avoid full refresh. We'll maintain the aggregate table incrementally and then refresh/concurrently for derived joins.

maya: Are we comfortable with eventual consistency in dashboards? quotas must be mostly real-time. We can't undercount for billing.

oliver: Good point — for billing/quota we continue to use the low-latency prefix/KV cache path. This MV is for console and analytics queries (dashboards, historical p99). For near-real-time console cards we can show streaming counts (approx) and then show MV as canonical after a minute.

raj: How about backfill and migration? previous attempts to backfill long time windows hit PG IO.

oliver: Plan: dual-write during rollout — write to existing envelope store + a write-optimized aggregator (Kafka topic -> materializer). Backfill using a cluster job that replays historical data into the aggregator with rate limiters and per-shard windows to avoid hotspots. Target: 48-72 hour backfill for last 90 days, doing slices by tenant shard.

sasha: Query patterns matter. For dashboards we need fast per-route top-k and p99. Recommend creating partial indexes for high-cardinality tenants and using pre-computed sketches for percentiles. Example partial index: `CREATE INDEX ON console.route_counters_minute (tenant_id, route_id) WHERE tenant_id = 'big-tenant';`

oliver: Agree. Also plan to expose retention policies: keep minute-level for 7d, hour-level for 90d, day-level for 2y. Materializer will compact older windows into coarser buckets.

maya: What about storage cost? If we shard too fine we explode row counts. Need an estimate and a read/write cost model before sign-off.

oliver: I'll run numbers. Rough estimate: current envelopes rows/month ~ 2B, after aggregation minute buckets expected rows ~ 30M (because sparsity), with compression + chunking should be manageable. I'll share a spreadsheet.

infra-bot: deploy-check: rolling out a materialized view + consumer requires infra approval for new topics and extra disk growth. Please file an infra ticket with estimated IO and retention.

raj: Operational concerns: who owns the aggregator? We'll need runbook for backfill pauses, replays, and failover. Also a way to reconcile counters if consumer reprocesses.

oliver: Ownership: eng-platform will ship, eng-sre will own runbooks for alerts (consumer lag, stuck compaction). For reconciliation: include a watermark and idempotent writes using (tenant_id, route_id, minute_bucket) key. We'll also emit reconciliation diffs for a sample of tenants nightly.

sasha: One more ask — dashboards that used JOINs on route metadata will need a compatibility layer: either join at query time to a lightweight route_lookup table or denormalize route meta into the counters table during materialization. I'd prefer denorm for performance.

oliver: Agreed. We'll denorm common route metadata (display_name, plan_tier) at write time with periodic sync.

maya: Ok—can we get a short RFC with the DDL, backfill plan (shards/slices), cost estimates, and runbook? Then schedule a quick sync with infra & eng-sre.

oliver: On it. Will post RFC by EOD tomorrow and ping @sasha for indexes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
